items.name: EQ_MAX_BANDS
items.doc: The maximum number of parametric bands a channel EQ may hold — the operator can add up to this many. Generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_EQ_MAX_BANDS`, which `omx_biquad.h` reads (the engine's conformance test reads the header): the native lane allocates exactly this many biquad slots per channel and silently clamps above it, so the model, the wire, and the DSP agree by test, not by memory.

items.name: ISO_THIRD_OCTAVE_CENTRES_HZ
items.doc: The standard ISO 266 one-third-octave centre frequencies, 20 Hz–20 kHz (31 bands) — the classic 31-band graphic-EQ layout's centres.

items.name: GEQ_BANDS
items.doc: The graphic EQ's section count: DERIVED from ISO_THIRD_OCTAVE_CENTRES_HZ, never a second literal. Generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_GEQ_BANDS`, which sizes `mix_geq.h`'s section array — its OWN budget, never a claimant on EQ_MAX_BANDS (roster ruling 3).

items.name: EQ_FREQ_RANGE
items.doc: The frequency band a parametric band can be dragged across.

items.name: EQ_GAIN_RANGE
items.doc: The parametric-band gain travel, in dB. The ± scalar `clampEqGain` enforces is READ off this (the engine derives its gain limit from `max`), so the bound is stated once and a surface cannot draw a wider knob than the clamp will honour.

items.name: EQ_Q_RANGE
items.doc: The Q (resonance) extent of a parametric band.

items.name: EQ_NOTCH_Q_RANGE
items.doc: The Q extent of a NOTCH band. Wider than EQ_Q_RANGE on purpose (#116, operator decision): an ultra-narrow surgical cut is the notch shape's whole point — the FBS ring-out pool plants dbx-AFS-style ring killers at Q ≈ 116 (~1/80 octave), inaudible on program yet fatal to a single ringing frequency. Gain-carrying shapes stay bounded at EQ_Q_RANGE — a Q-116 bell is a resonator, not an EQ move.

items.name: HPF_FREQ_RANGE
items.doc: Where the HPF cutoff can sit (low end); mirrors the drawn low-frequency handle.

items.name: LPF_FREQ_RANGE
items.doc: Where the LPF cutoff can sit (high end).

items.name: OPERATOR_EQ_BANDS_RESERVE

source.origin: the console engine's operator EQ bands reserve; read by omx-dsp 6d6fcda test/kernels/biquad.c

items.doc: The band slots kept for the operator's own hand: the reserve the feedback suppressor and the ring correction may never eat into. Nine is the working set a live EQ actually holds. The budget OPERATOR_EQ_BANDS_RESERVE + FBS_DEFAULT_MAX_AUTO_BANDS + HRP_DEFAULT_MAX_AUTO_BANDS (9 + 6 + 8 = 23) must fit EQ_MAX_BANDS, and `omx-contract validate` refuses data where it does not.

items.name: EQ_BAND_TYPES

source.origin: the console engine's EQ band types and their labels; omx-dsp 6d6fcda include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h enum omx_eq_lv2_type; omx-plugins 3778732 the eq decls' band type values

items.doc: The generic EQ band shapes, in the order a picker offers them and in the order of the integer a plugin host sees on a band type port. The id is the name; the position is the value. A bell is the shape a band added by the operator starts as.

items.name: FILTER_SLOPES

source.origin: the console engine's EQ filter slopes; omx-dsp 6d6fcda include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h enum omx_eq_lv2_slope

items.doc: The pass-filter slopes the EQ offers, in dB per octave. The id is the slope: 12 is one maximally flat section, 24 the two-section Butterworth.

items.name: EQ_BAND_COUNTS

source.origin: the console engine's default EQ state (four bands) and its maximum band count; omx-plugins 3778732 plugins/omx-strip/omx_strip.h OMX_STRIP_EQ_BANDS and plugins/omx-eq{8,16,32}/omx_eq*_stereo.h OMX_EQ_LV2_BANDS

items.doc: How many bands each strip type's EQ starts with (`default`) and may hold (`max`). `channel` is the console's channel strip: it starts with four and the operator adds bands up to EQ_MAX_BANDS (a band added takes the frequency it is added at, so no default is declared for it). `strip` is the omx-strip plugin's EQ and `eq8`, `eq16` and `eq32` the omx-eq plugins, whose bands are fixed. A default may never exceed its maximum, and the default centres of any count come from the one default rule, whatever the strip.

items.name: EQ_BAND_DEFAULTS

source.origin: omx-plugins 3778732 plugins/omx-strip/omx-strip.decl.json (eq bands: gain 0, Q 1 for bells and shelves); the console engine's default EQ state (gain 0)

items.doc: What every band of a fresh EQ comes up at, whatever its type and its strip: flat (0 dB) and Q 1. The band frequencies and types come from the default rule.

items.name: EQ_PASS_FILTER_DEFAULTS

source.origin: the console engine's default EQ state; omx-dsp 6d6fcda include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h OMX_EQ_LV2_HPF_FREQ_DEFAULT and OMX_EQ_LV2_LPF_FREQ_DEFAULT

items.doc: The corners the high-pass and low-pass filters of a fresh EQ are parked at, whatever the strip. Both come up off.

items.name: EQ_DEFAULT_CENTRES_FOUR_BAND_HZ

source.origin: operator ruling 2026-10-08 (omx-plugins' omx-strip set; the console follows it)

items.doc: The default band centres of a four-band EQ, Hz: ISO 266 preferred values, two to two and a half octaves apart. The default rule gives every other band count its centres from the preferred series; four bands start here.

items.name: EQ_CENTRE_SERIES_R20_HZ
items.doc: The ISO 266 R20 preferred frequencies from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (61 values, sixth-octave spacing): the finer series the default band rule falls back to where R10 (ISO_THIRD_OCTAVE_CENTRES_HZ, 31 values) has too few to give every band its own centre. R10 is a subset of it.

items.name: EQ_HPF_ONS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h:358-359 the hpf_on word, read at :386 with default 0; the console engine's default EQ state has the high-pass off; omx-plugins 7461cdd plugins/omx-eq8/omx-eq8.decl.json hpf_on (def 0)

items.doc: The HPF's switch: off, the filter is not in the EQ's bank at all; on, its one or two Butterworth sections run after the bands. It comes up off, on the console's channel EQ and in omx-dsp's EQ face (see EQ_PASS_FILTER_DEFAULTS).

items.name: EQ_LPF_ONS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h:358-359 the lpf_on word, read at :389 with default 0; the console engine's default EQ state has the low-pass off; omx-plugins 7461cdd plugins/omx-eq8/omx-eq8.decl.json lpf_on (def 0)

items.doc: The LPF's switch: off, the filter is not in the EQ's bank at all; on, its one or two Butterworth sections run after the bands and the HPF. It comes up off, on the console's channel EQ and in omx-dsp's EQ face (see EQ_PASS_FILTER_DEFAULTS).

items.name: EQ_BAND_ONS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_eq_instance.h:110 struct omx_eq_lv2_band.on, the fifth band word at :360, read at :399 with default 0; the console engine's default EQ bands are on; omx-plugins 7461cdd plugins/omx-eq8/omx-eq8.decl.json b<N>_on (def 0)

items.doc: A band's switch. Off, the band is not in the EQ's bank (the slots close up); on, it runs, parked when it is a gain-carrying shape at 0 dB. A band comes up off (operator ruling, 2026-10-13): an omx-eq plugin brings every band up off so a racked instance is a wire, and the console's channel EQ reads its come-up value here. A stored session keeps its own band states; only a fresh band comes up off.

items.name: LOWPASS_HANDOVER

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed include/omxdsp/omx_eq_design.h:44-60 OMX_EQ_LOWPASS_HANDOVER_Q_HI 0.70710678118654752, _Q_LO 0.54119610014619698, _LO_AT_Q_HI 0.6, _HI_AT_Q_HI 0.85, _LO_AT_Q_LO 0.8, _HI_AT_Q_LO 0.9, _Q_PEAK 0.9, _HI_AT_Q_PEAK 0.8; the console engine's core eq.ts:496-498 LOWPASS_HANDOVER_Q_HI, _Q_LO, _Q_PEAK and :509-511 the band ends 0.6, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9 and 0.8 inline

items.doc: Where the low-pass section hands its poles over from the matched pair to the prewarped bilinear pair, as fractions of Nyquist, and how that band moves with Q. At `qHi` (1/sqrt(2), the 12 dB Butterworth) the band runs from `loAtHiQ` to `hiAtHiQ`; at `qLo` (0.5412, the low-Q half of the 24 dB Butterworth) and below, from `loAtLoQ` to `hiAtLoQ`; between the two it moves linearly. Above `qHi` the prototype peaks, and the band's end moves down to `hiAtPeakQ` by `qPeak`, held above it. Below the band the low-pass is the matched design unchanged.
